- Calming pacing suitable for reading aloud before sleep, ending on a peaceful note
- Keep it to 300-450 words
If the user writes in Hindi, respond in Hindi; otherwise respond in English.

title: Plot Twist Generator
preview: Generate unexpected, logical plot twists for an existing story.
prompt:
Act as a story editor known for twist endings. Here is my current story or premise: [STORY SUMMARY]. Generate 5 possible plot twists that:
- Are genuinely surprising but feel inevitable in hindsight (recontextualize something already shown, don't come from nowhere)
- Each work with a different type of twist (identity reveal, hidden motive, false assumption, timeline shift, reversal of power)
- Include a one-line explanation of what earlier detail the twist recontextualizes
Rank the 5 by how strong they are, with a one-sentence reason for the top pick.

title: Genre Story Generator (Thriller / Romance / Mystery / Sci-Fi)
preview: Generate a genre-accurate story that hits the tropes readers expect.
prompt:
Act as a genre fiction specialist. Write a story opening (500-700 words) in the [GENRE — thriller / romance / mystery / sci-fi / horror] genre, based on this premise: [PREMISE]. Requirements:
- Hit the genre's expected tone and pacing from the first paragraph
- Include at least one signature element readers expect from this genre (e.g. a ticking clock for thriller, a meet-cute for romance, a clue for mystery, a world-altering concept for sci-fi)
- Introduce the central tension by the end of the opening
- Close with a hook line that would make a reader turn the page

title: Story Continuation Writer
preview: Continue an existing story while matching its exact tone and style.
prompt: Act as a ghostwriter matching an existing author's voice. Here is the story so far: [PASTE EXISTING STORY TEXT]. Continue it for the next 400-600 words. Before writing, briefly note (in one line) the tone, tense, and POV you detected, then continue seamlessly in that same style. Do not restart, summarize, or change the POV/tense. Advance the plot meaningfully — don't just describe the current scene further.

title: Moral / Motivational Story Generator
preview: Create a short moral story that teaches a value through narrative, not a lecture.
prompt:
Act as a storyteller in the tradition of Panchatantra and Aesop's fables. Write a short moral story that teaches this value: [VALUE — e.g. honesty, hard work, patience]. Requirements:
- Use characters (human or animal) and a simple, relatable conflict
- Let the moral emerge naturally through what happens to the characters — do not state the moral until the very last line
- Keep the language simple enough for students to follow
- End with a one-line moral, clearly marked
If the user requests it in Hindi, write the full story in Hindi.

title: Micro-Fiction / Flash Fiction Generator
preview: Generate a complete story in under 150 words with a real emotional punch.
prompt:
Act as a flash fiction writer. Write a complete story in under 150 words based on: [TOPIC/PROMPT]. Constraints:
- It must have a beginning, a shift, and an ending — a full arc, not just a scene
- Every sentence must earn its place; cut anything that doesn't move the story or land the emotion
- The final line should re-contextualize or land the story's meaning
After the story, state the exact word count.

title: Screenplay Scene Writer
preview: Write a properly formatted screenplay scene from a story idea.
prompt:
Act as a professional screenwriter. Convert this scene idea into proper screenplay format: [SCENE IDEA]. Use standard formatting:
INT./EXT. LOCATION - DAY/NIGHT
Action lines in present tense, describing only what's seen or heard
CHARACTER NAME centered above dialogue
Dialogue that reveals character through word choice, not exposition dumps
Keep action lines lean — screenplay convention is show, don't narrate. Limit to one scene, roughly 1-2 pages.

title: Poetry Generator
preview: Write an original poem in any style, form, or mood.
prompt:
Act as a skilled poet. Write an original poem about: [TOPIC/THEME]. Requirements:
- Choose a form that fits the theme (free verse, sonnet, haiku series, etc.) and state which you chose
- Use concrete, sensory imagery instead of abstract statements — show the feeling through detail, don't name it directly
- Vary line length and rhythm deliberately, not just for rhyme
- Avoid greeting-card clichés ("time heals", "love conquers all") unless deliberately subverting them
End with the strongest possible closing line — it should land, not just stop.

title: Fairy Tale Remix Generator
preview: Retell a classic fairy tale with a fresh, modern twist.
prompt:
Act as a creative writer who reimagines classic stories. Take this fairy tale: [FAIRY TALE NAME] and retell it with this twist: [TWIST — e.g. modern setting, villain's POV, different ending]. Requirements:
- Keep the core recognizable elements so readers still see the original underneath
- Commit fully to the twist — don't hedge back to the original halfway through
- Give it a clear beginning, middle, and end (400-600 words)
- Land on an ending that feels earned by the twist, not just different for its own sake

title: Villain Backstory Generator
preview: Build a compelling antagonist origin story that makes their villainy make sense.
prompt:
Act as a character writer specializing in antagonists. Create a backstory for a villain based on this concept: [VILLAIN CONCEPT]. Cover:
- The specific moment or betrayal that started their turn (not a vague 'hard childhood')
- What they believe about themselves — most villains think they're the hero of their own story; state their internal justification
- One quality they had before that they've twisted into something dark
- A moment where they could have turned back, and why they didn't
End with a single line of dialogue that captures their worldview.

title: Story Setting & Atmosphere Generator
preview: Generate a vivid, sensory-rich setting description for any scene.
prompt:
Act as a descriptive fiction writer. Write a setting description for: [LOCATION/SCENE], with this mood: [MOOD — e.g. eerie, cozy, tense]. Requirements:
- Use at least 3 different senses (not just visual)
- Choose 3-4 specific, unusual details rather than generic ones (not 'old house' but what makes THIS house feel that way)
- Let the mood emerge through word choice and detail selection, not by stating the mood directly
- Keep it to 150-250 words — dense and vivid, not padded

title: Choose-Your-Adventure Story Starter
preview: Generate the opening scene and first decision point for an interactive story.
prompt:
Act as an interactive fiction writer. Create the opening of a choose-your-own-adventure story based on: [PREMISE]. Structure:
1. Write an opening scene (200-300 words) that establishes the protagonist, setting, and an immediate situation requiring a decision
2. Present exactly 2 distinct choices at the end, each leading to meaningfully different consequences (not just cosmetic differences)
3. For each choice, write 1-2 sentences hinting at what kind of story path it leads to, without giving away the outcome
Keep the tone consistent with the premise throughout.

title: Blog Post Outline Generator
preview: Generate a structured, SEO-friendly outline for any blog topic.
prompt:
Act as a content strategist. Create a detailed blog post outline for the topic: [TOPIC], targeting this audience: [AUDIENCE]. Include:
- A compelling, specific headline (not generic — should promise a clear benefit)
- An introduction hook approach (question, stat, story, or contrarian claim)
- 4-6 main sections with descriptive subheadings
- Under each subheading, 2-3 bullet points of what to cover
- A conclusion approach that includes a clear call-to-action
Note where a stat, example, or quote would strengthen a section, without inventing fake data.

title: Email Newsletter Writer
preview: Write an engaging email newsletter that people actually want to open and read.
prompt:
Act as an email marketing copywriter. Write a newsletter email about: [TOPIC/UPDATE], for an audience of: [AUDIENCE]. Requirements:
- Write 3 subject line options (under 50 characters, no clickbait or ALL CAPS)
- Open with a personal, conversational line — not 'Hi there, hope you're well'
- Keep paragraphs short (1-3 sentences) for scannability
- Include one clear call-to-action, stated once but reinforced naturally
- End with a sign-off that matches a warm, human tone, not corporate

title: Book / Movie Review Writer
preview: Write a thoughtful, well-structured review for any book or film.
prompt:
Act as a culture critic. Write a review of: [BOOK/MOVIE TITLE]. Structure:
- Open with a one-line hook capturing your overall take, not a plot summary
- Briefly set up the premise without spoilers (2-3 sentences)
- Discuss what works — be specific (a particular scene, technique, or performance), not just 'great acting'
- Discuss what doesn't work, with the same specificity
- Close with who this would appeal to and a clear verdict
Avoid generic praise words like 'amazing' or 'incredible' — say exactly what earned the reaction.

title: Speech Writer
preview: Write a compelling speech for any occasion, from toasts to keynotes.
prompt:
Act as a speechwriter. Write a speech for this occasion: [OCCASION — e.g. wedding toast, graduation, keynote], about: [TOPIC/HONOREE]. Requirements:
- Open with a hook — a short story, question, or surprising fact, not 'Thank you all for being here'
- Structure around 2-3 clear points, each supported by a brief specific example or anecdote
- Write for the ear, not the eye — short sentences, natural rhythm, easy to say out loud
- Close with a memorable final line that ties back to the opening
Target length: roughly [DURATION] minutes when spoken aloud.

title: Social Media Content Calendar Generator
preview: Generate a full week of varied, on-brand social media post ideas.
prompt:
Act as a social media strategist. Create a 7-day content calendar for: [BUSINESS/BRAND], on this platform: [PLATFORM]. For each day, provide:
- Post type (educational, behind-the-scenes, promotional, engagement/question, testimonial, etc.) — vary types across the week, don't repeat the same type twice in a row
- A specific post idea/topic, not generic
- A one-line caption starter or hook
- Suggested format (image, carousel, video, text-only)
Ensure only 1-2 of the 7 days are directly promotional; the rest should build trust or engagement.

title: Sales Page Copy Writer
preview: Write persuasive, conversion-focused sales page copy from scratch.
prompt:
Act as a direct-response copywriter. Write sales page copy for: [PRODUCT/SERVICE], targeting: [TARGET CUSTOMER]. Structure:
1. Headline that states the core benefit or outcome
2. Sub-headline that addresses the main objection or adds specificity
3. 3-4 paragraphs agitating the problem, then introducing the solution
4. A bulleted list of 4-5 benefits (not features) using 'so that you can...' framing
5. A short testimonial-shaped placeholder section
6. A clear call-to-action with urgency that feels honest, not manipulative
Keep the tone confident but not hypey — no excessive exclamation points or ALL CAPS.

title: Influencer Outreach Message Writer
preview: Write a personalized, non-spammy outreach message to creators or influencers.
prompt:
Act as an influencer marketing manager. Write an outreach message to a content creator about: [COLLABORATION IDEA], for this brand: [BRAND]. Requirements:
- Open by referencing something specific about their actual content (leave a placeholder [SPECIFIC DETAIL] for the sender to fill in) — never generic flattery
- Clearly state what you're proposing and what's in it for them, not just the brand
- Keep it short — under 120 words, this isn't a sales page
- End with a low-pressure, easy next step (not 'let me know ASAP!!')

title: Brand Voice & Tone Guide Generator
preview: Define a clear, consistent brand voice with concrete do/don’t examples.
prompt:
Act as a brand strategist. Create a brand voice guide for: [BRAND/BUSINESS], based on this personality: [PERSONALITY — e.g. friendly expert, bold and irreverent, calm and premium]. Provide:
- 3 core voice traits, each with a one-line definition
- For each trait, one 'we sound like this' example sentence and one 'not like this' example sentence
- A short list of words/phrases the brand should avoid
- A short list of words/phrases that reinforce the brand's personality
Keep the whole guide practical enough that someone else could write on-brand copy from it alone.

title: Code Refactoring Assistant
preview: Get clean, well-explained refactoring suggestions for messy code.
prompt:
Act as a senior software engineer doing a code review. Here is my code:

[PASTE CODE]

Refactor it for readability and maintainability. Requirements:
- Preserve the exact original behavior — do not change functionality
- Explain each significant change and why it improves the code (naming, structure, duplication, etc.)
- Flag anything that looks like a potential bug, even if unrelated to the refactor, separately
- If the language/framework has an idiomatic convention being violated, point it out
Provide the refactored code in a single block, followed by a bullet list of changes made.

title: API Documentation Writer
preview: Generate clear, developer-friendly documentation for an API endpoint.
prompt:
Act as a technical writer specializing in developer documentation. Write API documentation for this endpoint:

[PASTE ENDPOINT DETAILS — method, path, params, response]

Include:
- A one-line description of what the endpoint does
- Request parameters in a table (name, type, required, description)
- A sample request (with realistic example values, not just placeholders)
- A sample successful response (realistic JSON)
- Common error responses and what causes them
Write for a developer integrating this for the first time — assume no prior context.

title: Regex Pattern Generator
preview: Get a working regex pattern with a plain-English breakdown of how it works.
prompt:
Act as a regex expert. Write a regular expression that matches: [WHAT TO MATCH — describe in plain English, with 2-3 example strings that should match and 1-2 that should NOT match]. Provide:
- The regex pattern itself
- A plain-English, piece-by-piece breakdown of what each part does
- Confirmation that it correctly matches your positive examples and rejects your negative examples
- Note any edge cases it might not handle, and what would be needed to cover them
Specify the regex flavor if relevant (e.g. JavaScript, Python, PCRE) — default to JavaScript if unspecified.

title: Database Schema Designer
preview: Design a normalized relational database schema from a plain description.
prompt:
Act as a database architect. Design a relational database schema for this application: [APP DESCRIPTION — describe what it does and the main entities involved]. Provide:
- A list of tables with their columns, data types, and primary/foreign keys
- Relationships between tables (one-to-many, many-to-many, with junction tables where needed)
- Which fields should be indexed and why
- Any normalization trade-offs worth flagging (e.g. deliberate denormalization for performance)
Present the schema as a clear list per table, followed by a short summary of the relationships.

title: SWOT Analysis Generator
preview: Generate a clear, specific SWOT analysis for any business or idea.
prompt:
Act as a business strategy consultant. Create a SWOT analysis for: [BUSINESS/IDEA], in this market: [MARKET/INDUSTRY]. For each of Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, and Threats, provide 3-4 specific points — not generic statements like 'strong brand' but concrete reasons why. Requirements:
- Weaknesses and Threats should be honest, not softened
- Opportunities should be realistic and actionable, not wishful
- After the four quadrants, add a 2-3 sentence summary of the single most important strategic implication

title: Business Plan Executive Summary Writer
preview: Write a sharp, investor-ready executive summary for a business plan.
prompt:
Act as a business plan consultant. Write an executive summary for: [BUSINESS IDEA]. Cover, in order:
1. The problem being solved (1-2 sentences, specific)
2. The solution and what makes it different
3. Target market and size, if known
4. Business model — how it makes money
5. Traction or key milestone, if any
6. The ask (funding, partnership, etc.), if relevant
Keep the whole summary under 300 words — this should work as a standalone pitch even if no one reads further.

title: Pitch Deck Outline Generator
preview: Generate a proven slide-by-slide structure for an investor pitch deck.
prompt:
Act as a startup pitch coach. Create a slide-by-slide outline for a pitch deck for: [STARTUP IDEA]. For each of these slides — Title, Problem, Solution, Market Size, Product, Business Model, Traction, Competition, Team, Ask — provide:
- What that slide should communicate in one sentence
- The single most important piece of information/data it needs to include
Keep notes concise — this is a structural outline, not full slide copy. Flag any slide where real data (market size, traction numbers) is essential and shouldn't be estimated.

title: Weekly Planning Template Generator
preview: Build a personalized weekly planning structure based on your priorities.
prompt:
Act as a productivity coach. Create a weekly planning template based on these priorities: [LIST YOUR TOP 3-5 PRIORITIES/GOALS FOR THE WEEK]. Structure it as:
- A Monday planning ritual (3-4 questions to answer before the week starts)
- A suggested time-blocking approach for the priorities (which days/times, not exact clock times)
- A mid-week check-in prompt (Wednesday) to catch drift early
- A Friday review ritual (what got done, what didn't, why)
Keep it flexible enough to actually stick to, not an overly rigid schedule.

title: Decision-Making Framework Assistant
preview: Work through a hard decision with a structured framework instead of gut-feel.
prompt:
Act as a decision-making coach. Help me think through this decision: [DESCRIBE THE DECISION AND THE OPTIONS]. Walk through:
1. Clarify what's actually being decided and by when
2. List the real criteria that matter for this decision (not generic ones)
3. For each option, briefly score it against those criteria
4. Identify what information is still missing that would most change the decision
5. Name the biggest risk of each option and whether it's reversible
End with a clear recommendation and the reasoning behind it — but flag it as a recommendation, not the final word.

title: Instagram Reel Script Generator
preview: Write a scroll-stopping short-form video script with hooks and pacing.
prompt:
Act as a short-form video scriptwriter. Write a 30-45 second Reel/TikTok script about: [TOPIC], for this niche: [NICHE/ACCOUNT TYPE]. Structure:
- Hook (first 1-2 seconds) — must stop the scroll, state a bold claim, question, or visual promise
- 3-4 quick beats delivering the value, each with a one-line visual/action note
- A close that either delivers a payoff or a clear call-to-action (follow, comment, save)
Write it as spoken lines with [VISUAL: ...] notes alongside, not a formal script format.

title: YouTube Video Description Writer
preview: Write an SEO-friendly video description that helps your video get discovered.
prompt:
Act as a YouTube SEO specialist. Write a video description for a video about: [VIDEO TOPIC], with this main keyword: [TARGET KEYWORD]. Structure:
- First 2 lines: a compelling hook that includes the main keyword naturally (this is what shows before 'more')
- A short paragraph summarizing what the viewer will learn/see
- A timestamps placeholder section
- 3-5 relevant hashtags at the end
- A call-to-action to subscribe, placed naturally, not as a separate demand
Keep the keyword usage natural — no keyword stuffing.

title: YouTube Channel Content Strategy Planner
preview: Plan a month of video topics aligned to a clear channel strategy.
prompt:
Act as a YouTube channel strategist. Create a content plan for a channel about: [CHANNEL NICHE/TOPIC], for the next 4 weeks. For each week, provide:
- One 'pillar' video idea (deeper, cornerstone content)
- One or two lighter/quicker video ideas that support the pillar topic
- The core viewer question or problem each video addresses
Group the ideas so they build on each other across the month rather than being random topics, and flag which video has the strongest potential to attract new (non-subscriber) viewers.

title: Study Guide Creator
preview: Turn any topic or notes into an organized, exam-ready study guide.
prompt:
Act as a study coach. Create a study guide for: [TOPIC/SUBJECT], based on this material if provided: [NOTES/TEXTBOOK CONTENT]. Structure:
- Key concepts organized under clear headings, most important first
- For each concept, a plain-language explanation plus one memory aid (analogy, acronym, or example)
- A short list of likely exam-style questions to self-test with
- A 'commonly confused' section flagging concepts students often mix up
Keep explanations clear enough for someone encountering the topic for the first time.

title: Personal Budget Planner
preview: Build a realistic monthly budget based on your actual income and expenses.
prompt:
Act as a personal finance coach. Help me build a monthly budget based on: income of [MONTHLY INCOME], and these expenses: [LIST KNOWN EXPENSES]. Provide:
- A suggested budget breakdown using percentages (needs/wants/savings) adapted to my actual numbers, not a generic 50/30/20 without checking if it fits
- Flag any category that looks unusually high relative to income
- 2-3 realistic, specific suggestions to free up savings, based on what I listed
- A simple way to track this weekly without needing new software
Be practical, not preachy — no generic 'stop buying coffee' advice unless it's genuinely relevant to my numbers.

title: Investment Option Comparison Framework
preview: Compare investment options side-by-side using a clear, unbiased framework.
prompt:
Act as a financial analysis assistant (not a licensed advisor). Compare these investment options: [OPTION A] vs [OPTION B], for someone with this goal and time horizon: [GOAL/TIMEFRAME]. For each option, cover:
- Typical risk level and volatility
- Liquidity (how easily it can be accessed/sold)
- Rough historical return pattern, described in general terms, not specific predictions
- Tax considerations if relevant
End with factors the person should weigh given their stated goal — not a directive 'buy this one'. Clearly note this is educational, not personalized financial advice.

title: Interview Answer Coach (STAR Method)
preview: Turn a rough work story into a structured, compelling STAR interview answer.
prompt:
Act as an interview coach. Help me turn this experience into a strong interview answer using the STAR method: [DESCRIBE THE SITUATION/EXPERIENCE ROUGHLY]. Structure the answer as:
- Situation: brief context (2 sentences max)
- Task: what specifically was I responsible for
- Action: what I actually did — most detail should go here, in first person, specific actions not vague ones
- Result: the outcome, with a number or concrete detail if possible
Keep the full answer to roughly 90 seconds of spoken length, and flag if my original story is missing a clear result I should think about.

title: LinkedIn Headline & About Section Writer
preview: Write a compelling LinkedIn headline and About section that gets noticed.
prompt:
Act as a personal branding coach. Write a LinkedIn headline and About section for someone with this background: [ROLE/EXPERIENCE/SKILLS], targeting: [WHAT THEY WANT — e.g. new job, clients, network]. Provide:
- 3 headline options (under 220 characters), each with a different angle (results-focused, expertise-focused, mission-focused)
- An About section (150-200 words) that opens with a hook, not 'I am a [job title] with X years of experience'
- The About section should read like a person talking, not a resume in paragraph form
End with a one-line call-to-action for the About section.

title: SEO Keyword Research Assistant
preview: Generate a structured list of keyword ideas and search intent for any topic.
prompt:
Act as an SEO strategist. Generate keyword ideas for the topic: [TOPIC/NICHE]. Provide:
- 8-10 keyword ideas grouped by search intent (informational, commercial, navigational, transactional)
- For each keyword, note the likely intent and what kind of content would satisfy it
- Flag 2-3 long-tail variations that are likely lower competition but still relevant
- Suggest one content angle that could realistically rank versus obvious/oversaturated angles
Note clearly that exact search volume/competition data should be verified in a real keyword tool — this is directional, not measured data.

title: Data Insight Summarizer
preview: Turn a raw data description or table into clear, actionable insights.
prompt:
Act as a data analyst. Here is a summary of my data: [DESCRIBE THE DATA OR PASTE A TABLE]. Analyze it and provide:
- 3-4 key insights, each stated as a clear takeaway, not just a restated number
- For each insight, note what action it suggests, if any
- Flag any surprising or counter-intuitive pattern
- Note any obvious data quality concern (missing values, small sample size, outliers) that should caveat the insights
Write for a non-technical audience — no jargon like 'p-value' or 'variance' without a plain-English explanation.

title: Python Function Docstring Generator
preview: Generate clean, standards-compliant docstrings for any Python function.
prompt:
Act as a Python developer following best practices. Write a docstring for this function:

[PASTE FUNCTION CODE]

Use Google-style docstring format, including:
- A one-line summary of what the function does
- Args section with each parameter's type and purpose
- Returns section describing the return type and meaning
- Raises section if the function can raise exceptions
- A short example usage if the function's behavior isn't obvious from the signature alone
Do not change the function's code — only add the docstring.

title: Literature Review Summarizer
preview: Synthesize multiple sources into a structured literature review summary.
prompt:
Act as a research assistant. Help me synthesize these sources into a literature review section on: [RESEARCH TOPIC]. Sources: [LIST SOURCE SUMMARIES OR KEY FINDINGS FROM EACH]. Structure the output as:
- Group sources by theme or finding, not just list them one by one
- For each theme, summarize what the sources agree on and note any disagreement between them
- Identify the gap in existing research that my own work could address
Write in an academic but readable tone. Do not fabricate citations or findings not provided in the source list.

title: Original Song Concept & Theme Generator
preview: Develop an original song concept — theme, mood, and structure — to write from.
prompt:
Act as a songwriting collaborator. Help me develop an original song concept about: [THEME/EMOTION/EXPERIENCE], in this genre: [GENRE]. Provide:
- A core emotional angle the song should center on (not just the topic, but the specific feeling)
- A suggested song structure (verse/chorus/bridge count) typical for the genre
- 2-3 possible hook/chorus concepts (the central idea, not full lyrics) to build around
- A few concrete images or metaphors that fit the theme, to spark original lines
Do not write full lyrics — this is a concept and structure guide for the user to write their own original lyrics from.

title: Cold Outreach Email Writer
preview: Write a short, personalized cold email that gets replies instead of ignored.
prompt:
Act as a B2B sales copywriter. Write a cold outreach email to: [TARGET ROLE/COMPANY TYPE], about: [WHAT YOU'RE OFFERING]. Requirements:
- Subject line under 6 words, specific and non-salesy
- Open with something clearly about THEM, not your company (leave a placeholder [SPECIFIC DETAIL ABOUT THEM])
- State the value proposition in one sentence, focused on their likely problem
- Keep the whole email under 100 words
- End with a low-friction call-to-action (a question, not 'let's hop on a 30-min call')
No hype words like 'revolutionary' or 'game-changing'.

title: Personalized Workout Plan Generator
preview: Build a structured weekly workout plan matched to your goals, level, and equipment.
prompt:
Act as a certified personal trainer. Design a weekly workout plan based on: goal of [GOAL — e.g. muscle gain, fat loss, general fitness], experience level [BEGINNER/INTERMEDIATE/ADVANCED], available equipment [EQUIPMENT — e.g. gym, dumbbells only, bodyweight only], and [DAYS PER WEEK] days available. Provide:
- A weekly split (which muscle groups/focus on which days)
- For each training day, 5-7 exercises with sets, reps, and rest periods appropriate to the goal
- A brief note on progression (how to increase difficulty over the following weeks)
- 1-2 safety cues for the most technical exercises included
End with a reminder that this is general guidance, not a substitute for a doctor's clearance if the person has an existing injury or condition.

title: Home Workout Routine (No Equipment)
preview: Get a full bodyweight-only workout routine you can do anywhere.
prompt:
Act as a bodyweight fitness coach. Create a [DURATION]-minute home workout requiring no equipment, focused on: [FOCUS — e.g. full body, core, cardio]. Structure:
- A 3-5 minute warm-up sequence
- The main circuit: 5-8 exercises with reps or time (e.g. '30 seconds on, 15 off'), organized so consecutive exercises don't overload the same muscle group
- Number of rounds through the circuit
- A 3-5 minute cool-down/stretch sequence
Include one easier and one harder variation for the two most difficult exercises, so it works for different fitness levels.

title: Weekly Meal Prep Planner
preview: Plan a week of balanced meals designed for efficient batch cooking.
prompt:
Act as a meal prep coach. Create a weekly meal prep plan based on: dietary preference [PREFERENCE — e.g. vegetarian, high-protein, no restrictions], and [NUMBER] meals to prep. Provide:
- 3-4 base recipes chosen so they share overlapping ingredients (to reduce shopping list length and waste)
- A simple batch-cooking order (what to cook first, what can cook simultaneously)
- Storage guidance (how many days each component keeps, fridge vs freezer)
- A consolidated shopping list grouped by grocery store section
Keep recipes realistic for a home kitchen — no professional equipment or rare ingredients.

title: Detailed Trip Itinerary Planner
preview: Build a realistic day-by-day itinerary for any destination and trip length.
prompt:
Act as a travel planner. Create a [NUMBER]-day itinerary for [DESTINATION], for someone interested in [INTERESTS — e.g. history, food, nature, nightlife], with a [BUDGET LEVEL — budget/mid-range/luxury] budget. For each day, provide:
- A logical geographic grouping of activities (don't zigzag across the city)
- Morning, afternoon, and evening suggestions with realistic timing
- One 'don't miss' recommendation per day tailored to the stated interests
- A note on local transport between areas
Flag 1-2 days as flexible/lower-key to avoid over-scheduling, and mention anything that typically needs advance booking.

title: Smart Packing List Generator
preview: Generate a complete, trip-specific packing list so you never forget essentials.
prompt:
Act as a travel packing expert. Create a packing list for a [DURATION]-day trip to [DESTINATION], during [SEASON/WEATHER], for [TRIP TYPE — e.g. business, beach vacation, hiking trip]. Organize into categories:
- Clothing (with realistic quantities based on trip length and laundry access assumptions)
- Toiletries and health items
- Documents and money
- Electronics and adapters (note the destination's plug type/voltage if known)
- Trip-specific gear based on the trip type
Flag anything that's easy to forget but commonly needed (e.g. a portable charger, sunscreen, or destination-specific items like mosquito repellent).

title: Cognitive Bias Identifier
preview: Spot the cognitive biases that might be influencing a decision or belief.
prompt:
Act as a decision-science coach. Here is a decision or belief I'm working through: [DESCRIBE THE SITUATION AND YOUR CURRENT THINKING]. Help me by:
- Identifying 2-3 cognitive biases that could plausibly be influencing my thinking (e.g. confirmation bias, sunk cost fallacy, anchoring), explained in plain terms specific to my situation, not a generic definition
- For each bias, a pointed question I could ask myself to check if it's actually affecting me
- One alternative way of framing the decision that removes the bias's influence
Be direct, not just validating — the goal is a clearer decision, not reassurance.

title: Habit Formation Coach
preview: Design a realistic plan to build a new habit that actually sticks.
prompt:
Act as a behavior-change coach grounded in habit science. Help me build this habit: [DESIRED HABIT]. My past attempts and where they usually break down: [DESCRIBE PAST ATTEMPTS, IF ANY]. Provide:
- A 'tiny version' of the habit small enough that skipping it feels harder than doing it
- A specific trigger/cue to attach it to (an existing routine, not just 'every day')
- One likely failure point based on my past attempts, and a concrete way to design around it
- A simple way to track consistency without it becoming its own burden
Focus on the smallest sustainable version, not the most ambitious one.

title: Personal SWOT / Self-Assessment
preview: Get a structured self-assessment to clarify your strengths and growth areas.
prompt:
Act as a career/life coach. Help me build a personal SWOT analysis. Here's context about me: [BACKGROUND, ROLE, RECENT CHALLENGES OR GOALS]. Guide me through:
- Strengths: prompt me to think beyond skills to include things like relationships, reputation, or resources
- Weaknesses: ask a pointed question that helps surface a real gap, not a humble-brag weakness
- Opportunities: what's changing around me (in my field, life stage, market) that I could take advantage of
- Threats: what could realistically derail my progress if ignored
After each section, ask ME the reflective question rather than just filling it in yourself — I'll provide the answer, then you can help me synthesize it.

title: SMART Goal Setting Framework
preview: Turn a vague ambition into a clear, trackable SMART goal.
prompt:
Act as a goal-setting coach. Help me turn this vague goal into a SMART goal: [VAGUE GOAL, e.g. 'get healthier', 'grow my business']. Walk through:
- Specific: what exactly does success look like, precisely
- Measurable: what number or clear marker will tell me I've achieved it
- Achievable: a sanity check on whether the timeline/scope is realistic given my situation (ask me for context if needed)
- Relevant: why this goal actually matters to me right now
- Time-bound: a specific deadline or checkpoint schedule
End with the final SMART goal statement in one clear sentence, plus the first concrete action to take this week.

title: User Journey Map Generator
preview: Map out a user’s full journey through a product to spot friction points.
prompt:
Act as a UX researcher. Create a user journey map for this scenario: [USER GOAL, e.g. 'signing up for a subscription', 'returning a product']. For the product/context: [PRODUCT/APP DESCRIPTION]. Map out, stage by stage:
- The stage name (Awareness, Consideration, Onboarding, Usage, etc. — adapt to fit the scenario)
- What the user is doing and thinking at each stage
- Their likely emotion at each stage (frustrated, confident, confused, etc.)
- The biggest friction point or drop-off risk at each stage
End with the single highest-impact stage to fix first, and why.

title: Usability Test Script Writer
preview: Write a moderator script for running a usability test session.
prompt:
Act as a UX researcher preparing a usability test. The product/feature being tested: [PRODUCT/FEATURE]. The goal of this test: [WHAT YOU WANT TO LEARN]. Write a moderator script including:
- A brief intro script to read to participants (setting expectations, reminding them to think aloud)
- 3-5 realistic tasks for the participant to attempt, written as scenarios not instructions (don't tell them exactly which buttons to click)
- 2-3 follow-up questions per task to probe their reasoning
- A closing set of 3 wrap-up questions about their overall impression
Avoid leading language anywhere in the script (e.g. don't say 'try the easy checkout' — just say 'checkout').

title: Design System Component Checklist
preview: Get a thorough checklist for what a reusable UI component needs to cover.
prompt:
Act as a design systems lead. Create a completeness checklist for this UI component: [COMPONENT — e.g. button, modal, form input]. Cover:
- All the states it needs (default, hover, active, focus, disabled, error, loading, etc. — as relevant to this component)
- Responsive/size variants it should support
- Accessibility requirements (keyboard navigation, ARIA attributes, color contrast)
- Content guidelines (character limits, what copy should/shouldn't go in it)
Format as a checklist a designer or developer could tick through before considering the component 'done'.

title: MVP Feature Prioritization Framework
preview: Decide which features actually belong in your MVP versus later releases.
prompt:
Act as a product strategy advisor. Help me prioritize features for an MVP of: [PRODUCT IDEA]. Here's my current feature list: [LIST FEATURES]. For each feature, evaluate:
- Is it solving the core problem, or a nice-to-have adjacent to it?
- Could the MVP work without it, even if imperfectly?
- Estimated build effort (low/medium/high) versus its impact on validating the core hypothesis
Sort features into 'Must have for MVP', 'Fast follow', and 'Later/maybe never'. End with a one-sentence description of what the leanest possible version of this MVP would be.

title: Startup Idea Validation Checklist
preview: Stress-test a startup idea before investing serious time or money.
prompt:
Act as a startup advisor who's skeptical by default. Here's my startup idea: [DESCRIBE THE IDEA]. Stress-test it by asking:
- Who exactly has this problem badly enough to pay for a solution, specifically (not 'everyone')
- What are they doing today instead, and why would they switch
- What's the cheapest possible way to test demand before building anything
- What's the most likely reason this idea fails, based on similar ideas you're aware of
Be honest, not encouraging for its own sake — if the idea has a real hole, say so plainly and explain why.

title: Freelance Proposal Writer
preview: Write a winning freelance proposal that stands out from generic pitches.
prompt:
Act as a freelance business coach. Write a project proposal for this job posting/brief: [PASTE JOB DETAILS OR DESCRIBE THE PROJECT], from a freelancer with this background: [YOUR RELEVANT EXPERIENCE]. Structure:
- Open by referencing something specific from their brief (proves you actually read it) — not a generic greeting
- Briefly show you understand the real problem behind their request, not just the surface task
- 2-3 sentences on relevant experience, with a specific result if you have one
- A clear next step (not just 'let me know')
Keep it under 150 words — avoid restating their entire brief back to them.

title: Freelance Rate Calculator Guide
preview: Work out a sustainable freelance rate based on your real costs and goals.
prompt:
Act as a freelance business consultant. Help me calculate a sustainable rate. My inputs: desired annual income [AMOUNT], expected billable hours per week [HOURS], business expenses (software, taxes, insurance, etc.) [EXPENSES IF KNOWN], and unpaid time to account for (admin, marketing, time off) [ESTIMATE OR ASK ME]. Walk through:
- The calculation logic step by step (don't just give a number — show the math)
- How much buffer to add for non-billable time and slow periods
- A sanity check against typical market rates for [FIELD/NICHE], if you have general knowledge of that
End with a suggested hourly and project-based rate, noting these are starting points to adjust with experience.

title: Workflow Automation Planner
preview: Map out how to automate a repetitive task using no-code tools.
prompt:
Act as an automation consultant familiar with tools like Zapier, Make, and n8n. Here's a repetitive task I do manually: [DESCRIBE THE TASK STEP BY STEP]. Help me automate it by providing:
- The trigger (what starts the automation)
- Each step as an 'action', in order, noting which app/service would handle it
- Any point where a decision/branch is needed (if X then Y, else Z)
- What still needs a human check, if anything, and why full automation might be risky there
Keep the plan tool-agnostic where possible, but note if a specific tool is clearly the best fit for a step.

title: Color Palette Concept Generator
preview: Generate a cohesive color palette concept with the reasoning behind it.
prompt:
Act as a visual designer. Suggest a color palette for: [PROJECT — e.g. brand, app, website], with this desired feeling: [MOOD/PERSONALITY — e.g. calm and trustworthy, bold and energetic]. Provide:
- A primary color and why it fits the mood
- 1-2 secondary/accent colors and their intended use (CTAs, highlights, etc.)
- A neutral color set for backgrounds and text
- One note on accessibility (ensuring sufficient contrast between text and background choices)
Describe colors precisely enough to look up (approximate hex families or clear names like 'deep forest green'), since you can't render swatches directly.

title: Twitter/X Thread Hook Generator
preview: Generate scroll-stopping opening lines for a Twitter/X thread.
prompt:
Act as a Twitter/X growth writer. Generate 8 hook options for a thread about: [THREAD TOPIC]. Requirements:
- Cover different hook styles: a bold claim, a surprising stat/fact, a question, a personal story opener, a listicle promise ('7 things I wish I knew...'), and a contrarian take
- Each hook must work as a standalone first tweet — someone should want to click 'show more' without any other context
- Keep each under 200 characters
- No generic openers like 'Let's talk about...' or 'A thread on...'
Mark which 2 you'd personally lead with and briefly say why.

title: AI Video Script Generator (Faceless Channel)
preview: Write a full narration script for a faceless YouTube video.
prompt:
Act as a scriptwriter for faceless YouTube channels. Write a narration script for a video about: [TOPIC], targeting roughly [DURATION] minutes. Structure:
- A hook (first 10-15 seconds) that states what the viewer will get and why it matters, without a slow intro
- 3-5 main sections, each with a clear sub-point, written in a natural spoken tone (not an essay read aloud)
- Suggested [B-ROLL: ...] notes at key moments to guide visuals
- A closing that reinforces the main takeaway and includes a subscribe call-to-action that doesn't feel forced
Write in short, punchy sentences suited for voiceover pacing, not dense paragraphs.

title: Sales Objection Handling Script
preview: Get ready-to-use responses for common sales objections.
prompt:
Act as a sales coach. Here's an objection I keep hearing: [OBJECTION — e.g. 'it's too expensive', 'I need to think about it', 'we already use a competitor']. For selling: [PRODUCT/SERVICE]. Provide:
- What the objection usually really means underneath the surface statement
- A response that acknowledges the concern genuinely before addressing it (not a dismissive 'I understand, but...')
- A specific question to ask that moves the conversation forward rather than just defending your position
- One thing NOT to do in response to this objection (a common mistake reps make)
Keep the tone consultative, not pushy.

title: Discovery Call Question List
preview: Generate a structured question set for an effective sales discovery call.
prompt:
Act as a B2B sales trainer. Create a discovery call question list for selling: [PRODUCT/SERVICE], to this type of buyer: [BUYER ROLE/COMPANY TYPE]. Organize into:
- Context questions (understand their current situation/setup)
- Pain/problem questions (surface the cost of not solving this)
- Goal questions (what does success look like for them)
- Decision-process questions (who else is involved, what's the timeline, budget signals)
For each section, include 2-3 open-ended questions (not yes/no) that invite the buyer to talk, not questions that sound like an interrogation.

title: Interview Question Bank Generator (For Hiring Managers)
preview: Generate a structured set of interview questions for hiring a specific role.
prompt:
Act as a hiring manager and recruiter. Create an interview question bank for hiring a: [ROLE], at this level: [SENIORITY]. Provide:
- 3 questions to assess core technical/functional skill for this role, with what a strong answer would include
- 2 behavioral questions (using situations, not hypotheticals) to assess soft skills relevant to the role
- 1 question specifically designed to surface red flags for this type of role
- 1 good closing question that reveals genuine interest versus a generic answer
Note which questions are must-ask versus nice-to-have if time is short.

title: Product Launch Email Sequence
preview: Plan a multi-email sequence to build hype and drive sales for a launch.
prompt:
Act as an e-commerce email marketer. Plan a launch email sequence for: [PRODUCT], launching on [DATE/TIMEFRAME]. Provide a sequence of 4 emails:
1. Teaser (before launch) — builds curiosity without revealing everything
2. Launch announcement — clear, benefit-led, with a strong CTA
3. Social proof/FOMO follow-up — reinforces why people are buying
4. Last-chance reminder — creates genuine urgency (only if there's a real deadline or limited stock)
For each email, give the subject line and a 2-3 sentence summary of the body content — not full copy, a structural plan.

title: Brand Naming Generator
preview: Generate original brand name ideas with the reasoning behind each.
prompt:
Act as a naming/branding strategist. Generate 12 name ideas for: [BUSINESS/PRODUCT DESCRIPTION], with this desired feeling: [TONE — e.g. playful, premium, trustworthy]. Group them into approaches:
- Descriptive names (hint at what it does)
- Evocative/metaphorical names (suggest a feeling or association)
- Invented/coined names (made-up but pronounceable)
- Compound names (two words combined)
For your top 3 picks across the list, note why they work and flag if a name might have an obvious downside (hard to spell, sounds like an existing brand, etc.). Remind the user to check trademark and domain availability before committing.

title: Competitor Analysis Framework
preview: Systematically analyze a competitor to find your differentiation angle.
prompt:
Act as a competitive strategy analyst. Help me analyze this competitor: [COMPETITOR NAME/DESCRIPTION], for my business: [YOUR BUSINESS]. Structure the analysis around:
- What they clearly do well (their apparent strengths, based on what's publicly known)
- Where they likely fall short (gaps in their offering, target audience they underserve, or common complaints if known)
- Their apparent positioning and pricing strategy
- A specific differentiation angle I could take that doesn't just copy them
Be honest that this is based on publicly observable information, not insider data, and flag anything that should be verified directly.

title: Ghostwriting Style Matcher
preview: Analyze a writing sample and write new content that matches the same voice.
prompt: Act as a ghostwriter. Here is a sample of someone's writing: [PASTE WRITING SAMPLE]. First, briefly describe the voice in 3-4 traits (e.g. short sentences, dry humor, uses rhetorical questions, avoids jargon). Then write a new piece on this topic: [NEW TOPIC], matching that exact voice as closely as possible. After the new piece, note any places where you had to make a judgment call about how the original writer would phrase something, so I can double check it feels authentic.

title: Unit Test Generator
preview: Generate thorough unit tests for a function, including edge cases.
prompt:
Act as a software engineer focused on test coverage. Write unit tests for this function:

[PASTE FUNCTION CODE]

Using [TESTING FRAMEWORK — e.g. Jest, pytest, JUnit]. Requirements:
- Cover the main expected-use case
- Cover edge cases (empty input, null/undefined, boundary values, unexpected types if the language allows them)
- Cover at least one case that should throw/return an error, if applicable
- Use clear, descriptive test names that state what's being verified
After the tests, briefly note any part of the function's behavior that seems ambiguous or under-specified, since that often means a bug or missing requirement.

title: Mystery / Whodunit Plot Generator
preview: Build a fair-play mystery plot with clues, a red herring, and a satisfying reveal.
prompt:
Act as a mystery novelist. Build a whodunit plot outline based on this premise: [PREMISE — e.g. victim, setting, general situation]. Provide:
- The victim and the crime
- 4 suspects, each with a plausible motive and opportunity
- The actual culprit and their true motive
- 3 clues planted throughout that a careful reader could use to solve it (fair-play — no information hidden from the reader that the detective has)
- 1 red herring that misdirects without being unfair
End with how the reveal scene should play out — what makes the culprit's explanation satisfying rather than just a confession.

title: Buyer Persona Comparison Generator
preview: Compare 2-3 buyer personas side by side to sharpen who to target first.
prompt:
Act as a marketing strategist. I have multiple potential customer segments for: [PRODUCT/SERVICE]: [LIST 2-3 SEGMENTS]. Compare them side by side on:
- Urgency of their problem (how badly do they need a solution right now)
- Ability to pay and typical budget
- How easy they are to reach with marketing (channels, existing communities)
- Likely objections for each
End with a clear recommendation on which segment to prioritize first, and why chasing all of them at once would likely dilute the marketing message.
